summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Evergreen Care through the Model Catalog in the Console + Redwood API and Optimize recommendations. Main focus: selecting open-source models for inference (medical domain TTR), benchmarking latency and cost, and confirming compatibility for private (VPC) deployment. Customer raised questions about SOC2, KMS integration, model variant fallbacks, and quantization tradeoffs. Agreed next steps include sharing compatibility matrix, running benchmarks on customer prompts, and scheduling POC kickoff.
header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Time: 16:00 - 16:42 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (CTO, Evergreen Care), Samir Patel (Head of MLOps), Lina Gomez (Security Engineer)
Artifacts shared: model_catalog_v2.xlsx, benchmark_sheet (link: https://tinyurl.com/evg-bench-2026), security-deck.pdf
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya on the SE side. we wanted to show the model catalog flow and how picking open models + our benchmark profiles works.
00:14 Maya Ortiz: Thanks, Jordan. We're particularly interested in lower cost open models for clinical triage -- we want something fast under 200ms for short prompts but also accurate for clinical intent.
00:29 Priya Natarajan: Great. quick overview: in the console the model catalog lists verified profiles, the model card includes throughput, latency medians, and quantization compatibility. there are pre-filter tags like "medical-finetuned", "low-latency", and quant flags. note sometimes the auto-transcript says "K V cash" but it's actually KV cache.
00:52 Samir Patel: Can you show how you'd pick a model for a mix of short triage prompts and longer summarization? we do about 30 qps on peak.
01:07 Priya Natarajan: Sure. filter for sequence length and the short seq distribution. here we have a few open models we've curated — e.g., Llama-3-7B (redwood-quant-xx), Mistral-7B-instruct, and a medic-tuned-flan variant. for short prompts the 7B quantized variant gives best cost/latency, but for summarization accuracy drops a bit.
01:36 Jordan Lee: I'll also flag that we can route requests by policy. so short triage can go to the low-latency pool and longer jobs to a higher-accuracy model. if Dedicated or Private is selected you get isolated capacity and consistent p99.
01:56 Lina Gomez: Quick security question — how do you handle keys and encryption in Private? do you support customer KMS or HSM?
02:07 Priya Natarajan: Yes, Private supports customer KMS and HSM integrations, and audit logs are included. we also have RBAC and SSO (SAML). i pulled up the security deck in the console — see the SOC2 section.
02:26 Maya Ortiz: On the benchmarks, what's the right way to understand compatibility? we saw a compatibility matrix in the docs but not sure about quantization levels across hardware.
02:38 Priya Natarajan: Good question. the compatibility matrix maps model variants to quant profiles and supported kernels per hardware (A100, H100, Ampere X). it's in the model_catalog_v2.xlsx we shared. an example: some 4-bit quant profiles are supported on our XPU optimized runtime but may have slightly higher latency on older GPU kernels.
03:02 Samir Patel: Are the numbers in the catalog synthetic or measured on-real infrastructure?
03:10 Priya Natarajan: They are measured on Redwood infra and annotated with the test harness details — sequence length, batch sizes. we put a confidence score on each benchmark. for customer-specific numbers we run a quick bench with your prompt set.
03:25 Maya Ortiz: Can you run that with our prompts? we can provide a redacted set. also want to check privacy — will Redwood keep any prompt data?
03:36 Jordan Lee: For Hosted we retain minimal logs; for Dedicated/Private you control retention. we'll sign an addendum if needed. for the POC we can run tests without storing prompt content — Priya can run it in ephemeral mode.
03:55 Priya Natarajan: I'll note that in the action items. moving on, here's how Optimize suggests batching and quant profiles: it looks at your token distribution and suggests model+quant combos to hit cost targets while keeping latency SLO. example: switching from float16-7B to q4_0 on certain kernels yields about 2.8x cost reduction but p95 latency increases ~10-15% depending on batch.
04:28 Samir Patel: That tradeoff is fine as long as triage stays under 250ms p95. we need the exact p95 numbers.
04:36 Priya Natarajan: We'll run targeted bench for triage prompts and return detailed p50/p95/p99. also show CPU vs GPU offload impact.
04:49 Jordan Lee: during demo we'll also show model fallback — if low-cost model fails accuracy guardrails we auto-fallback to a higher-accuracy variant. that's part of our rollouts.
05:02 Maya Ortiz: Is there any pre-packaged medical model in the catalog or is it all generic open models?
05:09 Priya Natarajan: We have some medic-tuned variants and community-finetuned ones. we tag them and include evals. note: names sometimes get munged in transcripts, e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" becomes "Redwood dedicate" in the notes.
05:25 Samir Patel: About deployment: we likely need VPC or on-prem because of PHI. what's the lead time for Private?
05:32 Jordan Lee: For Private (VPC) we push a private control plane and can do on-prem deployments. lead time depends on integrations but for a standard VPC + KMS it's typically 4-6 weeks; on-prem longer. dedicated reserved capacity is faster.
05:50 Lina Gomez: Does Private handle audit logs and SAML SSO at the same retention we require? we need 7 years retention for some logs.
06:00 Priya Natarajan: We can configure retention via the console; long-term retention is part of an add-on. we'll include that in the security deck.
06:12 Maya Ortiz: Could you show the compatibility matrix for Llama-3 variants?
06:18 Priya Natarajan: Sure — scrolling — Llama-3-7B: q4_0 supported on our XPU kernel, expected p50 ~ 45ms on H100 for short prompts (seq 64, batch 1), p95 ~ 180ms. Llama-3-13B: higher quality but p95 jumps to ~420ms unless quantized and batched.
06:47 Samir Patel: Those numbers seem optimistic; are you measuring with prefix caching enabled? we often have repeated contexts so caching matters.
06:55 Priya Natarajan: Yes, these are with KV cache warm for repeated session patterns. cold start is different. also Optimize can suggest prefix caching to reduce tokens and lower cost.
07:10 Jordan Lee: I'll point out the Console has per-route model mapping. you can tag routes like /triage and route to the 7B quant pool and set fallbacks.
07:22 Maya Ortiz: For the POC we want to test end-to-end latency, throughput (30 qps burst), and accuracy on triage. also want cost estimates.
07:34 Jordan Lee: Understood. typical next step: we run a benchmark with your prompts against 2-3 candidate models and provide a cost/latency/accuracy table plus suggested config in Optimize.
07:44 Samir Patel: On the pricing side, how do you price quantized models vs float16?
07:50 Jordan Lee: For Hosted API it's per-token with discounts for quantized tiers; for Dedicated it's capacity-based. we'll send the pricing sheet.
07:59 Lina Gomez: Any compliance certifications you don't have? we need ISO 27001 and SOC2 — do you have both?
08:06 Priya Natarajan: We currently have SOC2 Type II; ISO is in progress. we'll share the compliance timeline and the SOC2 report under NDA.
08:18 Maya Ortiz: Great. can you also clarify model lineage and provenance? we need to know training data provenance for risk assessment.
08:26 Priya Natarajan: We include model cards with provenance notes where available, and flag community-finetuned models. for regulated workloads we recommend customer-finetuned models or Private deployments.
08:40 Jordan Lee: we'll include a model lineage spreadsheet in the compatibility packet — note some community models have partial lineage.
08:50 Samir Patel: If we go POC, will Redwood be able to demonstrate fallback behavior under load?
08:56 Priya Natarajan: Yes — we can run a chaos test where we throttle the 7B pool and show automatic routing to a higher-accuracy pool with minimal request errors.
09:08 Maya Ortiz: timeline question: once we sign POC, how fast can you run the benchmark? we ideally want results within a week.
09:16 Jordan Lee: If you provide prompts this week we can run an initial bench within 3 business days. full POC with instrumentation may take 2 weeks.
09:27 Samir Patel: For the bench, include cost per 1M tokens estimate and breakdown by token category.
09:34 Priya Natarajan: Will do. I'll also attach the bench harness config we use. link in chat: https://tinyurl.com/evg-bench-2026
09:44 Jordan Lee: any other questions on model catalog or the compatibility matrix?
09:49 Maya Ortiz: One last: how do you handle model updates and rollouts to avoid regressions?
09:56 Priya Natarajan: We have canary rollouts, A/B testing, and auto-fallback policies. plus quality monitoring with eval hooks so you can tie regressions to specific prompts.
10:10 Lina Gomez: okay, enough for now. please put the security docs in the same thread as the bench results.
10:16 Jordan Lee: will do. recap of next steps: Jordan sends compatibility matrix + pricing; Priya runs bench; Evergreen shares prompts and SLOs; schedule POC kickoff.
10:31 Maya Ortiz: thanks everyone, that was helpful. we'll follow up with the redacted prompts by Friday.
10:38 Jordan Lee: thanks all, talk soon.

Note: transcription contains a few recognition errors (product names, acronyms occasionally split). timestamps approximate every ~15-60s.
